_: The seed edit strategies. The live set (with scores and children) is automation/strategies.json, mirrored to MongoDB edit_strategies; this file only seeds it. See prompts/reference/strategies.md for what each knob means.

strategies.name: The house style
strategies.brief: The way films have been made so far, as prompts/match.md describes, with no extra rule. The baseline the others are measured against.
strategies.notes: Strategy #0: the films before strategies existed count toward this one.

strategies.name: Caster, straight to the kill

narration.persona: an esports caster calling it live: present tense, shouting at the big moments, hearts and pressure

strategies.brief: Esports energy. The very first thing on screen is the last second before the final blow (the leap, the swing), with the caster already mid-shout, cut on the blow itself so the result stays unknown; then rewind and show how it came to that. Fast talk, excited, every line about pressure and hearts. Dramatic finale song.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: a kill in the first two seconds keeps the swipe-happy viewer. Watch the retention curve's first 10%.

strategies.name: Deadpan, in order

narration.persona: a bored referee reading out what happened, unimpressed by everyone including the winner

strategies.brief: Dry, few words, let the picture be the joke. Tell it in order. The narrator sounds mildly unimpressed by everything, including the winner. The bouncy finale song.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: sparse dry narration reads as confident; good when something dumb happened.

strategies.name: The players tell it
strategies.brief: No narrator except one line at most. The film is carried by the players' own chat, spoken in their voices, the game's sound and the music. Open on a chat line. Needs a match where people actually typed.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: real player voices feel like being there; narration feels like a documentary.

strategies.name: What the kit does

narration.persona: a coach explaining to a new player exactly what each kit is for, from what just happened

strategies.brief: The kits are the characters. Every beat is explained through what a kit can do and the moment it did it; name the kits in the title. The viewer should leave knowing exactly what the winning kit is for.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: kit names are what Hardcore Games people search and share.

strategies.name: People, not classes

narration.persona: a short-story narrator: what someone wanted, what they did, what it cost; people, never classes

strategies.brief: A small story about people with names and wants; never say the word kit or a kit's name. What someone wanted, what they did, what it cost. Wide, calm shots; the dramatic finale song.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: a viewer who does not know the game stays for a story, not for mechanics.

strategies.name: Together until they were not

narration.persona: someone telling a friend about a couple they knew, fond and a little sad

strategies.brief: Two players who stuck together, told as a relationship: how they met, what they shared, and the moment it ended (a betrayal, a death, the rule that only one can win). Warm music first, the dramatic song at the end. Needs a real team-up in the data.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: the teaming drama is the most human thing in these matches.

strategies.name: Trailer: music first, few words

narration.persona: a film trailer voice: four or five lines, each one heavy

strategies.brief: Epic music from the first frame, four or five lines in the whole film, each one short and heavy. Open on the most physical moment there is (a leap, a hit, a fall). The picture and the music do the work.
strategies.notes: Hypothesis: on a phone with sound on, music carries better than talk.

strategies.name: Nature documentary

narration.persona: a nature documentary: the players are creatures observed in their habitat, their habits and instincts described gently and precisely; the winner is simply the one best adapted

strategies.brief: A nature documentary about the match. Observe the players as creatures: where they go, what they gather, how they hunt, how they hide. Never a game term, never a kit name; a stomp is a creature dropping on its prey from a height. Enchanting music to open, the dramatic song for the kill.
strategies.notes: Tabor's idea (2026-10-07): the narrator's point of view is its own variable. Hypothesis: a documentary frame makes the game legible to people who never played it.
